Provide citation/PMID and evidence.'}

The matching paper is **“[Waist-to-height ratio does not change with gender, age and pubertal stage in elementary school children]”**, *Revista Médica de Chile* (2014), **PMID: 25427013**.

It reports a **cross-sectional study** of 2,980 schoolchildren aged 6–14 years in Santiago, Chile (51% male). Pubertal stage was grouped as peripubertal (Tanner I–II) or pubertal (Tanner III–V). The authors concluded that WHtR did not vary by sex/gender, chronological age, or pubertal status. The reported age-adjusted WHtR association by gender and pubertal stage was not statistically significant (**p=0.409**); the abstract provides no separate age-specific WHtR estimate or p-value. The **p=0.5** reported in the abstract concerns mean age by gender, not WHtR. [[Article abstract and details](call_5r09mwSv6ZTTHk28P1fRXK5W); [search result](call_aVy65pPVhyxQy7ovqg9JDvvm)]

The retrieved evidence directly addresses the question: in this cross-sectional sample, the authors report no WHtR variation by sex, age, or pubertal stage, while the specific reported age-adjusted comparison was nonsignificant. **No—not in the study found.** A 2014 cross-sectional study of 2,980 children aged 6–14 in Santiago, Chile, reported that waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) did not vary by sex, age, or pubertal stage. The reported age-adjusted comparison by gender and pubertal stage was not statistically significant (p=0.409). The abstract does not provide a separate age-specific WHtR estimate or p-value, and a cross-sectional finding does not establish that WHtR never changes in other populations.
